draft.title: Interconnection
card: Interconnection means that people, places and environments are linked to one another. What happens in one can affect the others.
The links can join places that are far apart. A change in one place can have effects in another place a long way away.
Links can be made by people, such as trade, travel and the sending of information. They can also be made by nature, such as rivers carrying water downstream.
To study a problem, geographers ask what is linked to it and how a change in one part may reach other parts.
draft.remember: Places, people and environments are linked, so a change in one can reach another.

opts: Rain in the hills raises a river that floods a town below
A town has a library, a park and a swimming pool
A town sits 200 km from the nearest city
A town is much older than the one beside it
a.why: The rain in the hills changes the river, and that change affects a town in another place. The other options describe a town's features, its distance or its age, but none shows a change in one place affecting another.
a.clue: Look for a change in one place that reaches another place.

b.q: A drought cuts the wheat harvest on farms in Western Australia. Shops in a distant country then pay more for flour made from that wheat. Why is this an example of interconnection?
opts: A change in one place affected people in another place
The two places both grow wheat each year
The farms and the shops are the same distance apart
The drought was caused by people in the other country
b.why: The drought changed the harvest in one place, and that change reached shoppers far away through trade. The second option is wrong because the shops do not need to grow wheat for the link to exist. The last option is not stated and is not what makes it interconnection.
b.clue: Follow the change from the farms to the shops.

a.best: Rain in the hills raises a river that floods a town below

b.best: A change in one place affected people in another place

problems.detail: Why (b) points to options by position ('the second option', 'the last option'), but the options are shuffled and its labels already fail here. The 'second' option is about distance, not growing wheat. The 'last' option is about both places growing wheat, not the drought's cause. Name the options by content instead.

The distractor 'The farms and the shops are the same distance apart' makes no sense, because it does not say what they are the same distance from. Students may be confused rather than meeting a clear wrong answer. Reword it, for example 'The farms and the shops are close together'.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate and each has one clear right answer. Why (b) refers to options by position and mismatches the shuffled options. One distractor in (b), about distance, is worded confusingly.
